name: git_add_or_commit
description: Add file contents to the index (git add <pathspec>) OR record changes to the repository (git commit -m <message> [files...]). Use the 'action' parameter to specify which action to perform.

arguments.name: action
arguments.desc: The action to perform: 'add' or 'commit'

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: The directory to run git add or commit in

arguments.name: files
arguments.desc: Optional array of files to add or commit. If omitted, all files are added or all staged changes are committed.

arguments.name: message
arguments.desc: The commit message (required if action is 'commit')

name: git_blame
description: Show what revision and author last modified each line of a file (git blame <file>).

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: The directory to run git blame in

arguments.name: file
arguments.desc: The file to blame

name: git_branch
description: List or create branches (git branch).

arguments.name: action
arguments.desc: Git branch action to be executed

arguments.name: branch_name
arguments.desc: (Optional) Name of the branch to create or delete

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: The directory to run git branch in

name: git_checkout
description: Switch branches or restore working tree files (git checkout <branch>).

arguments.name: branch
arguments.desc: The branch to checkout. This must be a valid branch name without spaces

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: The directory to run git checkout in

name: git_fetch
description: Download objects and refs from another repository (git fetch).

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: The directory to run git fetch in

name: git_log_or_diff
description: Show commit logs or changes between commits (git log --oneline or git diff).

arguments.name: action
arguments.desc: The action to perform: 'log' for commit logs or 'diff' for changes

arguments.name: authors
arguments.desc: Optional array of author names or emails to filter commits by (only applies to 'log' action)

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: The directory to run the command in

arguments.name: revision_range
arguments.desc: Optional revision range (e.g., 'HEAD', 'main..feature', 'abc123', 'HEAD~5..HEAD'). For 'diff' action, shows differences for the specified range. For 'log' action, shows commits in the range. Defaults to HEAD.

arguments.name: since
arguments.desc: Optional date/timestamp/relative time to show commits after (e.g., '2024-01-01', '2 weeks ago', 'yesterday', '1 hour ago', '3 days ago'). Only applies to 'log' action.

arguments.name: until
arguments.desc: Optional date/timestamp/relative time to show commits before (e.g., '2024-12-31', '1 week ago', 'today', 'yesterday', '2 hours ago'). Only applies to 'log' action.

name: git_pull
description: Fetch from and integrate with another repository or a local branch (git pull).

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: The directory to run git pull in

name: git_push
description: Update remote refs along with associated objects (git push).

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: The directory to run git push in

name: git_stash
description: Stash the changes in a dirty working directory (git stash).

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: The directory to run git stash in

arguments.name: include_untracked
arguments.desc: When true, include untracked files in the stash.

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: Optional name for the stash (used as the stash message)

arguments.name: staged_only
arguments.desc: When true, stash only the currently staged changes and leave unstaged work untouched.

name: git_status
description: Show the working tree status (git status), will open a UI if client supports it.

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: Path of the working directory.

name: git_worktree
description: List or add git worktrees (git worktree <action>).

arguments.name: action
arguments.desc: Git worktree action to be executed

arguments.name: branch
arguments.desc: (Optional) Existing branch for the new worktree (used for add)

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: The directory to run git worktree in

arguments.name: path
arguments.desc: (Optional) Path for the worktree (required for add)

name: gitkraken_workspace_list
description: Lists all Gitkraken workspaces

name: gitlens_commit_composer
description: Gitlens Commit Composer. Organize your changes into well-formed commits with clear messages and descriptions. Useful for breaking large changes into smaller commits.

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: Path of the working directory.

arguments.name: instructions
arguments.desc: OPTIONAL. Use this ONLY if the user explicitly provided specific requirements about how commits should be organized, what commit messages should say, or particular commit structure preferences. Do NOT use this parameter unless you are 100% certain about the user's intentions. Examples: 'use conventional commits', 'prefix each commit with JIRA-123', 'keep commit messages under 50 characters'.

name: gitlens_launchpad
description: Gitlens Launchpad. Gets your open pull requests prioritized by what needs attention: ready to merge, has conflicts, awaiting review, etc. Helpful for checking todos, outstanding tasks, or deciding what to work on next.

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: Path of the working directory.

name: gitlens_start_review
description: Gitlens Start Review. Creates a dedicated worktree and reviews your PR with an AI agent.

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: Path of the working directory.

arguments.name: instructions
arguments.desc: OPTIONAL. Use this ONLY if the user explicitly provided specific requirements about the review focus, review criteria, or what aspects to check. Do NOT use this parameter unless you are 100% certain about the user's intentions. Examples: 'focus on security issues', 'check for performance regressions', 'review only the authentication logic'.

arguments.name: pr_url
arguments.desc: URL of the PR to start review.

name: gitlens_start_work
description: Gitlens Start Work. Creates a work based on an issue. This tool will create a branch and link it with the issue, keeping context visible throughout your work.

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: Path of the working directory.

arguments.name: instructions
arguments.desc: OPTIONAL. Use this ONLY if the user explicitly provided specific requirements about the implementation approach, or additional context to supplement the issue. Do NOT use this parameter unless you are 100% certain about the user's intentions.

arguments.name: issue_url
arguments.desc: URL of the issue to start work on.
